Graduate Admission Overview
We want your graduate admission process to be stress-free, and we are here to support you!
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering reviews all completed applications. Each piece of your application informs our admissions committee about what you can bring to the program and how our program can accentuate your skills and potential.

Graduate Application Requirements
All of our graduate programs require an online graduate application. Below are the required items necessary to complete your application.
Online Graduate Application
Begin your online application at https://gradadmissions.colostate.edu/apply/
Application Fee
There is a $60 non-refundable application fee for domestic students or a $70 fee for international students. The fee is submitted in the online graduate application.
While the CEE Department is not able to waive your application fee, CSU offers several opportunities to receive an application fee waiver. Visit the Graduate School’s page on ways to apply for free.
Short-Answer Questions
The application includes seven short-answer questions pertaining to your professional background, research interests, and other areas. Be sure to adhere to the word-count limit.
Statement of Purpose
The application requires a Statement of Purpose. You will follow a prompt in the application.
Three Recommendations
Identify three individuals who can speak to your abilities as a student, engineer, scientist, and/or researcher.
If you are currently a student, two of the three letters of recommendation should be from faculty.
The graduate application system will email the individuals you specify. Be sure to inform your references they will be receiving the automated email request so the message is not lost in spam.
Current Resume
Provide an up to date resume or curriculum vitae reflecting your educational, professional, and research experience, including any presentations and publications.
Transcripts
Our departmental Graduate Admissions Committee can use unofficial transcripts to review graduate applications and make admission decisions. Students must submit official transcripts before or during their first semester.
Unofficial Transcripts:
Upload unofficial transcripts from each college or university attended to the application portal. Transcripts must include all previous undergraduate and graduate work.
Transcripts must be provided in the native language. For languages other than English, English translations must be included.
Official Transcripts:
Students must submit their official transcripts from each institution they’ve attended to CSU Graduate Admissions before or during their first semester of classes.
Students have the option to deliver official transcripts to the Graduate School upon arrival to campus. You may request your to have your official transcripts returned to you after processing.
Current CSU students do not need to request CSU transcripts. Admissions will automatically attach your CSU transcript once your application is complete.
For more details, review the Graduate School’s information on how to submit official transcripts.
English Proficiency Scores (international applicants)
International applicants must meet CSU’s Graduate School English proficiency requirements.
Submit official original test scores as outlined at the website above (institution code 4075).
Check Your Application Status
If the Department recommends you for admission to a graduate program, you will be contacted by the Department to submit official transcripts and documentation to CSU.
Check the status of your application at any time online at https://gradadmissions.colostate.edu/apply/
Steps Once Admitted
Once you are admitted (congratulations!), here are your next steps.

Applying Without a CEE Degree
Students who want to pursue a graduate degree in Civil and Environmental Engineering without a B.S. in Civil, Construction, or Environmental Engineering are required to complete additional background coursework in their area of specialization.
This coursework is not a prerequisite for admission: some students choose to complete these courses before applying to strengthen their application or reduce time-to-degree while others complete background courses after starting the program.
Your required background courses will depend on your undergraduate degree.
Master's Background Courses
Students without a B.S. degree in civil, construction, or environmental engineering will complete background courses for their intended specialization:
Water Resources, Hydrology, Hydraulics, and related graduate specializations:
CIVE 300 Fluid Mechanics (3 credits)
CIVE 322 Basic Hydrology (3 credits)
Structural Engineering, Solid Mechanics, and related graduate specializations:
CIVE 360 Mechanics of Solids (3 credits)
CIVE 367 Structural Analysis (3 credits)
Geotechnical, Geoenvironmental Engineering and related graduate specializations:
CIVE 355 Geotechnical Engineering (3 credits)
CIVE 360 Mechanics of Solids (3 credits)
Environmental Engineering and related graduate specializations:
CIVE 300 Fluid Mechanics (3 credits)
CIVE 339 Environmental Engineering Concepts (3 credits) OR CIVE 438 Fundamentals of Environmental Engineering (3 credits)
All other specializations:
Six or more upper-division CIVE credits (300-400 level), selected with your advisor to match your specialization
Additional Requirements
In addition to the background courses required for the specialization, students with a bachelor’s degree in a non-engineering field will be required to take the following foundational courses:
MATH 160, 161, and 261: Calculus for Physical Scientists I, II, and III (4 credits each, 12 credits total)
MATH 340: Introduction to Ordinary Differential Equations (4 credits)
PH 141 Physics for Scientists and Engineers I (5 credits)
CHEM 111 General Chemistry I (4 credits)
CIVE 260 Engineering Mechanics-Statics (3 credits)
CIVE 261 Engineering Mechanics-Dynamics (3 credits)
CIVE 300 Fluid Mechanics (3 credits)
CIVE 360 Mechanics of Solids (3 credits)
Completion of any prerequisite required for the courses listed above is also generally required.
Courses required of our undergraduates may not be used for graduate credit, including:
CIVE 401 Hydraulic Engineering (3 credits)
CIVE 466 Design and Behavior of Steel Structures (3 credits)
CIVE 467 Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures (3 credits)
Ph.D. Background Courses
All Ph.D. students, regardless of undergraduate degree, must complete:
MATH 160, 161, and 261 Calculus for Physical Scientists I, II, and III (4 credits each, 12 credits total)
MATH 340 Introduction to Ordinary Differential Equations (4 credits)
In addition, PhD applications must complete courses for their specialization:
Water Resources, Hydrology, Hydraulics, and related graduate specializations:
CIVE 300 Fluid Mechanics (3 credits)
CIVE 322 Basic Hydrology (3 credits)
Structural Engineering, Construction Engineering & Management, and related graduate specializations:
*CIVE 360 Mechanics of Solids (3 credits)
*CIVE 367 Structural Analysis (3 credits)
**A structural design course such as concrete
Geotechnical, Geoenvironmental Engineering and related graduate specializations:
CIVE 355 Geotechnical Engineering (3 credits)
Environmental Engineering and related graduate specializations:
***CIVE 300 Fluid Mechanics (3 credits)
**A 300- or 400-level environmental engineering course (3 credits)
*Competency in this subject may instead by demonstrated by exam.
**Specific course selected at your advisor’s discretion.
***Course requirement at your advisor’s discretion.
After You're Admitted: Process & Timeline
Students admitted with outstanding background courses will work with their faculty advisor to develop a plan for completing them:
Work with your faculty advisor to prepare a written plan identifying your specific background courses.
Submit the plan to the department for approval by the start of the registration period for your second semester.
Background courses must be taken for a traditional letter grade (not pass/fail) and count for credit.
Maintain an overall GPA of 3.0 in your background coursework. If you repeat a course, the highest grade earned counts toward this GPA.
Requesting a Course Waiver
With your advisor and graduate committee’s recommendation, you may petition the Department Head to waive specific background courses based on:
Extensive relevant experience
Completion of similar coursework elsewhere
A professional engineering (PE) license.
A Note for Engineering Technology Graduates
These background course requirements are in addition to your program’s normal graduate degree requirements. If your degree is in engineering technology, we encourage you to complete a B.S. in Civil Engineering before entering the graduate program.
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need to have a faculty advisor before applying?
No. You are not required to secure a faculty advisor prior to submitting your application materials.
Do you offer graduate assistantships?
Yes. Our Master of Science and Ph.D. students are frequently offered graduate teaching assistantships (GTA) or graduate research assistantships (GRA). These assistantships typically include full coverage of tuition along with a monthly stipend. Visit our assistantships page for more details.
We do not provide GTA or GRA funding to students seeking a Master of Engineering (coursework only) degree or graduate certificates. These students are generally self-funded. Review funding opportunities and options on the Graduate School webpage.
What criteria do you look for in graduate applicants? Can someone review my transcripts, test scores, or letters before I apply?
Our Graduate Admissions Committee considers applications holistically and will review all completed applications. We are not able to provide a preliminary review, but will fully review all completed graduate applications.
Do you require the GRE?
No. The GRE is no longer required by our department for admissions. Students who did take the GRE and have strong test scores may upload their test scores as supplemental materials to their application. Doing so may help strengthen your overall application package if your application has weak areas.
Are application fee waivers available?
The CSU Graduate School offers several ways to apply for free.
The CEE Department is NOT able to waive application fees.
What are the requirements to prove English proficiency? Is my country exempt? Which tests do you accept?
The English proficiency requirement is established by the CSU Graduate School, not by our department.
For the most current guidelines, visit https://graduateschool.colostate.edu/admissions-resources/english-proficiency/
If you do not meet the posted requirement, it is recommended you retake an English proficiency test.
Can I apply to the Ph.D. program if I have a bachelor's degree but not a master's degree?
Students who apply to the Ph.D. program without a master’s degree must have significant research and publication experience. If you do not have significant research and publication experience, please apply for the Master of Science degree.
I missed the application deadline! Can I still apply?
Students should not apply for admission past the final deadline unless a faculty member has offered you a Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA).
I'm interested in the joint Construction Management Ph.D. program - how should I apply?
Apply to the Ph.D. program in “Civil and Environmental Engineering” then under “Area of Interest/Study” you will indicate “Construction Management” on the application.
When asked to provide the names of 2-3 faculty you are interested in working with, be sure to include faculty from both CEE and CM Departments.
Note: Applicants to the joint Ph.D. program must have a prior master’s degree.
See more about our joint Construction Engineering and Management Ph.D. program.
